steps.context: Two engines on the same counts and design is the robustness check the procedure specifies at 2-11 replicates per group. The consolidated report is the deliverable that answers the research question.
steps.question: Does an independent engine agree on which genes carry a treatment-specific time response, and what is the high-confidence intersection?

grounding.reason: Two-method robustness with the intersection as the high-confidence set (R-0042); the report carries the fit diagnostics, the design and thresholds, the power statement, and the reproducibility record (R-0087, R-0041, R-0094, R-0086).

constraints: Use the same gene filter and the same design as T1S2 — the comparison is meaningless otherwise
TMM scaling factors go into the edgeR model as offsets; do not hand edgeR pre-normalized values
Do not report the union of the two methods as the answer

With a low-power interaction test, the ranked list is noisy at the top and enrichment results should be read as hypothesis-generating
steps.context: Counts.csv carries gene symbols in its first column, and the WikiPathways human GMT in the reference store uses HGNC symbols, so the identifier spaces match directly; report the share of tested genes that do not match a set-member symbol.

grounding.reason: Preranked enrichment on the full ranked list with a test-statistic metric, a 15-500 set-size window, redundancy collapsing, and the tested genes as universe (R-0045, R-0099, R-0047, R-0052, R-0046); human collection choice per R-0048 with WikiPathways confirmed present in the store.

constraints: Never run enrichment on a thresholded gene list — use the full ranked list
Use only human gene sets; the store also holds mouse and rat WikiPathways and using them here would be a species error
The ranking metric is the LRT statistic with an imposed sign, and this must be stated as a caveat, not presented as a signed test statistic
Do not use the whole genome as a background — for any over-representation side-analysis the universe is the genes tested in T1S2
steps.description: Take the full tested-gene list from T1S2 (every gene that survived the filter, not a thresholded subset), ranked by the DESeq2 LRT statistic. BH adjustment across the tested sets is applied and the random seed is stated
Redundant significant sets are collapsed to one representative per group, with the full table kept as a supplement
The share of ranked genes not matching any set member is reported
If no human pathway collection is available at run time, the step reports that explicitly instead of substituting a different organism's sets

plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE across t0-t3
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw salmon gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 24 samples in counts.csv, one column per sample) with a metadata table (24 x 4: sample, condition, time, time_hours) describing a 2-condition x 4-timepoint design with 3 replicates per cell. The research question — which genes change in a treatment-specific way over the four time points, beyond the shared time trend — is exactly an interaction question: the target is the condition:time term, not any single pairwise contrast. Because time has four levels, the interaction spans three coefficients, so the primary test is a DESeq2 likelihood ratio test of full ~ condition + time + condition:time against reduced ~ condition + time (this is the alternative the knowledge service names for a time course with three or more time points; the knowledge check flagged only that LRT differs from the Wald default, which is expected here). T1S1 runs the sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) so that a mis-labelled timepoint or an outlier replicate is seen before the model is fit. T1S2 fits the model and runs the LRT with a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest cell size), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and the p-value histogram as a fit diagnostic. T1S3 characterises the significant interaction genes: per-timepoint log2 fold changes versus t0 within each condition (the simple effects), apeglm/ashr-shrunken interaction coefficients, and clustering of the difference trajectories so the answer is a set of response shapes rather than a single fold change. T1S4 cross-checks with an independent engine (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design and the same filtered matrix) and reports the intersection as the high-confidence set. T1S5 is an optional interpretation step: preranked enrichment on the full tested gene list ranked by the LRT statistic against human WikiPathways, which is present in the reference store. Power is the central caveat: 3 replicates per cell, and an interaction coefficient is a difference of differences with a larger standard error than a main effect, so absence from the significant list is not evidence of a shared time trend. Every step must state this and must not loosen thresholds to compensate.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (smallest cell size)
~ condition + time + condition:time with explicit reference levels (condition reference = control arm, time reference = t0); power statement from replicates, depth and dispersion
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test, full ~ condition + time + condition:time vs reduced ~ condition + time; simple effects per condition reported beside
apeglm shrinkage of each condition:time interaction coefficient; ashr where a contrast is not a single coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with DESeq2 independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected first
Interaction report: simple effects at each condition level, interaction contrasts, trajectory clusters of significant genes, MA and dispersion plots, power statement, session info

steps.name: Preranked enrichment of the interaction signal

steps.description: Take the full tested-gene list from T1S2 (every gene that survived the filter, not a thresholded subset), ranked by the DESeq2 LRT statistic.
